title: Extensions of unitriangular-embeddable affine group schemes
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Groups are affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Write $\mathcal U_{n,k}\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group] for the group with upper triangular matrices having all diagonal entries $1$ as its $A$-points, for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$. Call a group unipotent if for some $n\geq1$ it admits a group homomorphism into $\mathcal U_{n,k}$ which is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $N\hookrightarrow E$ be normal and let $q:E\to Q$ represent the fppf quotient [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure], with scheme-theoretic kernel $N$: the quotient sheaf is the sheafification of $A\mapsto E(A)/N(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings. If $N$ and $Q$ are unipotent, then $E$ is unipotent. No smoothness, reducedness, connectedness, commutativity or perfectness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Section 6.45, printed p.135, extension argument using the normal-invariant space; Corollary 14.7, printed p.282; Theorem 14.5(a),(b), printed pp.281–282, identifies the representation-theoretic definition with the stated unitriangular embedding.

proof.text: Let $W\ne0$ be any finite-dimensional rational $E$-representation, meaning a homomorphism $E\to\operatorname{GL}(W)$. Choose a basis of size $d\geq1$ and restrict it to $N$. The assumed closed immersion of $N$ into a unitriangular group meets every hypothesis of [lem-sfb-unitriangular-subgroup-rational-fixed-vector]. It gives $0\ne v\in W$ fixed by $N$ after every commutative $k$-algebra extension. The representation-comodule dictionary identifies the action with a coaction and identifies this assertion with $c_N(v)=v\otimes1$.

source.place: Section 6.45, printed p.135: the nonzero normal-invariant vector; Theorem 14.5(b) implies (a), pp.281–282; Remark 4.1, p.84.

proof.text: By the quotient convention in [def-sfb-solvable-group-structure], the represented fppf quotient $q:E\to Q$ is flat and surjective with scheme-theoretic kernel $N$. Since $E$ and $Q$ are affine, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] makes $q^*:k[Q]\to k[E]$ a flat ring map, and surjectivity of $q$ is surjectivity of $\operatorname{Spec}k[E]\to\operatorname{Spec}k[Q]$. Hence $q^*$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-surjective-spectrum-faithfully-flat]: tensoring with $k[E]$ over $k[Q]$ is exact and detects zero modules, applying the exactness criterion to $0\to M\to0$. Apply [lem-sfb-central-kernel-cyclic-representation-descent] with $H=E$, $G=Q$, $K=N$ and the vector $v$ from step 1. The smallest rational $E$-submodule $W_0\subseteq W$ containing $v$ is nonzero and finite-dimensional, $N$ acts trivially on it, and its action descends to a rational $Q$-action whose pullback along $q$ is the original action. The cited lemma explicitly does not require the kernel to be central or reduced.

source.place: Section 6.45, p.135: factor the normal-invariant representation through the quotient; Lemma 5.15, p.102, and Theorem 5.13, p.101. Taking the cyclic submodule of a nonzero invariant vector suffices.

proof.text: Choose a basis of $W_0$, of size $e\geq1$. The finite-dimensional clause of [lem-sfb-rational-representation-comodule-dictionary] expresses its descended rational action as a homomorphism $Q\to\operatorname{GL}_{e,k}$. Since $Q$ admits a closed unitriangular immersion, [lem-sfb-unitriangular-subgroup-rational-fixed-vector] gives $0\ne w\in W_0$ fixed by $Q$ over every test algebra. For each $k$-algebra $A$ and $g\in E(A)$, the action of $g$ on $w\otimes1$ is the action of $q_A(g)$, hence is the identity. The inclusion $W_0\hookrightarrow W$ carries $w$ to a nonzero $E$-fixed vector. Thus EVERY nonzero finite-dimensional rational $E$-representation has a nonzero rational fixed vector.

source.place: Section 6.45, p.135: $(V^N)^{G/N}$ is nonzero and consists of $G$-fixed vectors; Remark 4.1, p.84.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-affine-group-faithful-linear-representation], choose $m\geq1$ and a closed immersion $r:E\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}$. Write $V=k^m$ for this representation. Its existence uses only that $E$ is affine and of finite type over the field $k$, not smoothness or reducedness.

source.place: Theorem 14.5(a) implies (b), p.281, invoking Theorem 4.9 and Corollary 4.10, p.87.

proof.text: Construct a flag in $V$ by induction on its dimension, using the fixed-vector property proved in steps 1–3. Dimension zero has the empty flag. In positive dimension choose a nonzero $E$-fixed vector $a$, and put $L=ka$. For every test algebra $A$, the action fixes $L\otimes_k A$ pointwise, so induces an action on $(V/L)\otimes_k A$: choosing a vector-space complement to $L$ identifies this tensor quotient, and the formula $g[x]=[gx]$ is independent of the representative and natural in $A$. It is a group action by linear automorphisms. The dictionary makes it a rational representation, and its dimension is one less. Induction supplies a complete flag with trivial one-dimensional successive actions on $V/L$. Its inverse images under $V\to V/L$, preceded by $0\subset L$, give a complete $E$-stable flag $0=V_0\subset V_1\subset\cdots\subset V_m=V$ with trivial action on each $V_i/V_{i-1}$. This construction uses the fixed-vector property for the same group $E$ on arbitrary representations; it does not assume that a quotient group is already unipotent.

source.place: Proposition 14.3, p.280, and Theorem 14.5(a) implies (b), p.281: the fixed-vector induction constructing a unipotent faithful representation.

proof.text: Choose a basis $a_1,\ldots,a_m$ with $V_i=\langle a_1,\ldots,a_i\rangle$. Flag stability and triviality of its successive actions give, for every $A$ and $g\in E(A)$, $r_A(g)a_j-a_j\in\langle a_1,\ldots,a_{j-1}\rangle_A$. Thus the matrix in this basis has entries zero below the diagonal and entries one on the diagonal. Apply this also to the universal point over $k[E]$: the corresponding matrix coefficients satisfy those equations in the coordinate algebra itself. Hence the basis-conjugated morphism $r':E\to\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}$ factors as $E\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal U_{m,k}\hookrightarrow\operatorname{GL}_{m,k}$. It remains a closed immersion after this factorization. Indeed conjugating by a fixed invertible matrix is an isomorphism, so $r'$ is a closed immersion. The coordinate map $k[\operatorname{GL}_m]\twoheadrightarrow k[E]$ is surjective and factors through the quotient $k[\mathcal U_m]$ by the stated matrix equations. The induced map $k[\mathcal U_m]\to k[E]$ is therefore surjective. The affine closed-immersion criterion in [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes $i$ a closed immersion. This proves exactly the required unitriangular embeddability over $k$.

source.place: Theorem 14.5(a) implies (b), p.281; Proposition 14.3, p.280; Stacks Tag 01QO (morphisms.tex, lemma-closed-immersion), affine criterion already included in def-weil-closed-immersion.

proof_origin.place: Section 6.45, p.135; Proposition 14.3, p.280; Theorem 14.5(a),(b), pp.281–282, with Theorem 4.9 and Theorem 5.13. The cyclic submodule version uses the same normal-invariant argument.
